advances: The new implication is a parity-and-sign injection: if all nonvertex positive-support sites lie in at most \(m\) affine flats, then the positive-support sites outside those flats number at most \(2^{n+m}\), independently of their ranks. A separating hyperplane for each occupied flat gives a binary sign coordinate; the midpoint of any distinct same-parity pair of outside sites lies in a covering flat and forces opposite signs in that coordinate. Combining this finite outside-site bound with actual lower-rank body slices converts the accepted polynomial coefficient into an absolute coefficient whenever the sum of the slice costs \(2^{r_i}(r_i+5)\) is at most \(B2^n\). This is a structural sufficient condition, not a restatement of the accepted bound in ambient dimension or a claim that every body has such a cover.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The only accepted inputs are the singleton specialization of the actual local transfer and its constant estimates in `0bcc51d8cd216cf3`, and the actual-body bound and depth attainment in `3bcbf21f33edf564`.
proof:
Compactness of the base projection of \(C\) makes \(D_+\) finite. All mixed volumes below are sums of the original \(d\)-dimensional fiber volumes. Thus zero-volume integer fibers contribute zero, but every positive-volume fiber is retained, including any fiber situated on a boundary of \(C\) or of a slice. No full-dimensionality of \(P\) is assumed.

Omit the empty occupied supports and reindex the remaining ones by \(1\leq i\leq k\), where \(0\leq k\leq m\). Since \(A_i\) is affine and contains \(E_i\), its occupied affine hull satisfies \(F_i\subseteq A_i\). Consequently \(D_+\cap F_i=E_i\), and replacing the covering flats by their occupied affine hulls changes neither their covered support sites nor their costs. Put
\(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^k E_i\) and \(O=D_+\setminus U\).
Every site in \(O\) is a vertex of \(P\). For each occupied flat choose \(\mathbf a_i\in E_i\), and write \(V_i=F_i-\mathbf a_i\) for its direction space.

First we prove \(|O|\leq2^{n+k}\). There is nothing to prove if \(O=\varnothing\). Otherwise every \(F_i\) is a proper affine subspace: a flat equal to \(\mathbb R^n\) would contain all of \(D_+\). For each \(\mathbf z\in O\), the linear form
\(\mathbf u\mapsto\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf z-\mathbf a_i)\) on \(V_i^\perp\) is nonzero, since \(\mathbf z\notin F_i\).
There exists \(\mathbf u_i\in V_i^\perp\) on which all these finitely many forms are nonzero. Here is an elementary justification of this simultaneous choice. For finitely many nonzero linear forms, inductively keep a vector where the preceding forms are nonzero. If the next form vanishes there, perturb along a vector where the next form is nonzero; the preceding forms forbid at most one scalar perturbation each, and the next form forbids the zero scalar. A real scalar outside this finite set completes the induction. In particular \(\mathbf u_i\ne\mathbf0\).
The affine function
\(\ell_i(\mathbf z)=\mathbf u_i\cdot(\mathbf z-\mathbf a_i)\) vanishes on \(F_i\) and never vanishes on \(O\). Its zero set is a proper affine hyperplane containing \(F_i\) and avoiding all outside sites.

Suppose distinct \(\mathbf z,\mathbf z'\in O\) have the same parity in \(\mathbb Z^n\). Their midpoint \(\mathbf b=(\mathbf z+\mathbf z')/2\) is an integer point of \(P\), hence belongs to \(D_+\) by lattice completeness. It is not a vertex, because it is a nontrivial convex combination of two distinct points of \(P\). The cover therefore puts \(\mathbf b\) in some \(E_i\subseteq F_i\). For that index,
\(0=\ell_i(\mathbf b)=(\ell_i(\mathbf z)+\ell_i(\mathbf z'))/2\).
Both endpoint values are nonzero, so they have opposite signs. Thus the map

\[
\mathbf z\longmapsto
\left(\mathbf z\bmod2,
\bigl(\operatorname{sgn}\ell_i(\mathbf z)\bigr)_{i=1}^k\right)
\]

is injective on \(O\), giving \(|O|\leq2^n2^k\). When \(k=0\), the same argument says that no distinct same-parity pair can exist: its nonvertex midpoint would have to lie in the empty cover. The empty sign code therefore causes no exception.

We next record the actual single-fiber bound used twice below. For \(\mathbf j\in D_+\), let \(\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}\) be the actual centroid of \(C_{\mathbf j}\). Apply the local-transfer conclusion (1) of accepted fact `0bcc51d8cd216cf3` to the singleton \(E=\{\mathbf j\}\). Its local depth \(\tau_E(\mathbf j)\) equals \(w_{\mathbf j}\), since every containing closed base halfspace includes the site. Its barycentric parameter \(\vartheta_{\mathbf j}(E)\) equals one. Therefore
\(h_S((\mathbf j,\mathbf c_{\mathbf j}))\geq\gamma_dw_{\mathbf j}\), where
\(\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d>1/e\).
The centroid belongs to the actual fiber. This accepted conclusion includes all containing halfspaces, not just those whose boundary passes through the centroid. The proper-base-halfspace convention in that fact is consistent with \(\tau_p\): adding the whole base space to an infimum cannot decrease it, since its mass is the total mass and every proper halfspace mass is at most that total.

If \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in O}w_{\mathbf z}\geq W/2\), then \(O\ne\varnothing\), and one of its sites \(\mathbf j\) satisfies

\[
w_{\mathbf j}\geq\frac{W}{2|O|}
\geq\frac{W}{2^{n+k+1}}
\geq\frac{W}{2^{n+m+1}}.
\]

Its actual fiber centroid consequently has depth at least
\((e2^{m+1})^{-1}2^{-n}W\), as required in this case.

It remains to consider \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in U}w_{\mathbf z}>W/2\). In this case \(k\geq1\). Write
\(K=24\sqrt{15}\ln2\), and for each occupied flat put
\(T_i=\sum_{\mathbf z\in E_i}w_{\mathbf z}>0\).
We prove that some actual point of \(S\) lying over \(F_i\) has depth at least
\(T_i/[K2^{r_i}(r_i+5)]\).

For \(r_i=0\), the occupied hull is a single integer point \(\mathbf a_i\), and \(T_i=w_{\mathbf a_i}\). The single-fiber bound already proved supplies depth at least \(\gamma_dT_i\), which is larger than \(T_i/(5K)\). Indeed \(\ln2=\int_1^2t^{-1}\,dt>1/2\), so \(5K>60>e\), using \(e<3\) as established in accepted fact `0bcc51d8cd216cf3`.

Now let \(r_i\geq1\). Since \(F_i\) is the affine hull of integer points, its direction space \(V_i\) contains \(r_i\) real-linearly independent integer differences. The saturated direction lattice
\(L_i=V_i\cap\mathbb Z^n\) has an integer basis \(\mathbf v_{i,1},\ldots,\mathbf v_{i,r_i}\) spanning \(V_i\). For completeness, this basis assertion follows by induction on \(n\) for any subgroup \(G\) of \(\mathbb Z^n\). Its projection to the first coordinate is either zero or \(a\mathbb Z\) with \(a>0\). In the zero case apply the induction to \(G\subseteq\{0\}\times\mathbb Z^{n-1}\). Otherwise choose \(\mathbf g\in G\) with first coordinate \(a\). Every element of \(G\) is uniquely an integer multiple of \(\mathbf g\) plus an element of the kernel of this projection, and induction gives a basis of that kernel. Appending \(\mathbf g\) gives a real-linearly independent integer basis of \(G\). Applied to \(L_i\), the real span is exactly \(V_i\), because it contains the independent integer differences just noted and is contained in \(V_i\). Its basis therefore has exactly \(r_i\) elements. Saturation means that if \(q\mathbf v\in L_i\) for \(\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^n\) and a nonzero integer \(q\), then \(\mathbf v\in V_i\), hence \(\mathbf v\in L_i\).

Define the affine bijection
\(\psi_i:\mathbb R^{r_i}\to F_i\) by
\(\psi_i(\mathbf t)=\mathbf a_i+\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}t_j\mathbf v_{i,j}\).
It maps \(\mathbb Z^{r_i}\) bijectively onto \(F_i\cap\mathbb Z^n=\mathbf a_i+L_i\).
The actual transformed slice is

\[
\widehat C_i=
\{(\mathbf t,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\times\mathbb R^d:
(\psi_i(\mathbf t),\mathbf x)\in C\}.
\]

This set is compact and convex: it is the inverse image of the compact convex intersection \(C\cap(F_i\times\mathbb R^d)\) under an affine homeomorphism. It is also full-dimensional in \(\mathbb R^{r_i+d}\), so it is a convex body to which the accepted actual-body theorem applies. To check this even when the ambient slice lies in a boundary or \(P\) has smaller dimension than \(n\), choose \(r_i+1\) affinely independent sites in \(E_i\). Every corresponding fiber contains a ball of positive radius: a positive-volume convex set has full affine hull, contains a full-dimensional simplex, and therefore contains a ball. Choose a common smaller positive radius for these finitely many balls. Convex combinations of the balls give a ball of that radius in each fiber over the interior of their base simplex, with center the affine interpolation of their centers. The set of points over the simplex interior whose distance from this interpolated center is less than that radius is a nonempty open subset of \(\mathbb R^{r_i+d}\) contained in \(\widehat C_i\).

Let \(\widehat S_i=\widehat C_i\cap(\mathbb Z^{r_i}\times\mathbb R^d)\), and let \(h_{\widehat S_i}\) be its locked halfspace depth in \(\mathbb R^{r_i+d}\). At an integer \(\mathbf t\), the slice fiber is exactly \(C_{\psi_i(\mathbf t)}\). Its positive integer support is exactly \(\psi_i^{-1}(E_i)\), and its total mixed volume equals \(T_i\). There is no lattice-covolume or Jacobian factor: the integer sites are counted bijectively and the continuous coordinate \(\mathbf x\) is unchanged. Empty fibers and nonempty zero-volume fibers remain allowed.

Apply the body conclusion (9) of accepted fact `3bcbf21f33edf564` with the explicit substitution
\((n,d,C,S,W)=(r_i,d,\widehat C_i,\widehat S_i,T_i)\).
It supplies \(\widehat{\mathbf y}_i\in\widehat S_i\), selected independently of a containing halfspace, with
\(h_{\widehat S_i}(\widehat{\mathbf y}_i)\geq T_i/[K2^{r_i}(r_i+5)]\).
Map this point to \(\mathbf y_i\in S\) by
\((\mathbf t,\mathbf x)\mapsto(\psi_i(\mathbf t),\mathbf x)\).

For every proper closed ambient halfspace \(H\ni\mathbf y_i\), its inverse image under this affine map is either a proper closed halfspace in \(\mathbb R^{r_i+d}\) or the whole space. It cannot be empty, since it contains \(\widehat{\mathbf y}_i\). This classification follows by restricting the defining affine inequality of \(H\): its linear part either remains nonzero or becomes zero. In the proper case its slice mixed volume is at least the depth lower bound just obtained. In the whole-space case that volume equals \(T_i\), which is also at least the bound. Moreover its mixed volume is exactly
\(\sum_{\mathbf z\in E_i}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf z}\cap H_{\mathbf z})\), and this is at most \(\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\). The equality retains positive-volume fibers on the boundary of a vertical halfspace in their entirety. No assumption that a boundary fiber has zero volume is made. If the whole ambient space is itself admitted as a closed halfspace, its mass is \(W\geq T_i\) and it satisfies the same bound. Taking the infimum over all containing ambient halfspaces proves
\(h_S(\mathbf y_i)\geq T_i/[K2^{r_i}(r_i+5)]\).

Thus this conclusion holds for every occupied flat, including rank zero. A weighted-average comparison gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{1\leq i\leq k}\frac{T_i}{2^{r_i}(r_i+5)}
&\geq\frac{\sum_{i=1}^k T_i}
{\sum_{i=1}^k2^{r_i}(r_i+5)}\\
&\geq\frac{\sum_{\mathbf z\in U}w_{\mathbf z}}{B2^n}
>\frac{W}{2B2^n}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The first inequality follows by multiplying the maximum by the sum of its positive denominators. The second uses \(\sum_i T_i\geq\sum_{\mathbf z\in U}w_{\mathbf z}\); overlaps can only increase the numerator. We do not allocate disjoint masses to the slices or sum their depths. The comparison merely selects one slice whose ratio is at least this weighted average, and the actual point supplied by that slice has depth at least \((2KB)^{-1}2^{-n}W\).

The two mass cases prove the claimed coefficient. It is positive because \(m\) and \(B\) are fixed and finite, and it is strictly less than \(1/e\) because \(m\geq1\) gives \(c(m,B)\leq1/(4e)\). The maximum is also literal: the depth-attainment argument for compact mixed-integer sets in accepted fact `3bcbf21f33edf564` applies to the original \(C,S\). In any event the construction already supplies a particular actual point attaining the asserted lower bound.

The rank budget requires no uniform bound on the individual ranks. Dividing it by \(2^n\) rewrites it as
\(\sum_i(r_i+5)2^{-(n-r_i)}\leq B\).
For example, it is sufficient that every occupied flat satisfy
\(2^{n-r_i}\geq(m/B)(r_i+5)\).
Equivalently, codimension at least \(\log_2(r_i+5)+\log_2(m/B)\) suffices, where \(\log_2 t=\ln t/\ln2\). The stronger sufficient inequality
\(2^{n-r_i}\geq(m/B)(n+5)\) shows directly that codimension growing only logarithmically with \(n\) can pay the polynomial factor. At the level of this cost inequality, for all sufficiently large \(n\) one may take \(r_i=n-\lceil\log_2((m/B)(n+5))\rceil\); these nonnegative ranks tend to infinity and satisfy the stronger sufficient inequality. These are sufficient cost comparisons, not existence statements for a cover.

Indeed, the covering hypothesis with this budget need not hold for arbitrary bodies. Fix \(n\) with \(n+5>B\), choose an integer \(R\geq2\) with \(2R-1>m\), and take \(d=1\) and \(C=[-R,R]^n\times[-1,1]\). Its positive support is all of \([-R,R]^n\cap\mathbb Z^n\), and every site of the interior grid \(\{-R+1,\ldots,R-1\}^n\) is a nonvertex of \(P=[-R,R]^n\). Any proper affine flat is contained in a hyperplane with some nonzero coordinate coefficient. Fixing the other \(n-1\) coordinates leaves at most one possible value of that coordinate, so the flat contains at most \((2R-1)^{n-1}\) sites of this grid. At most \(m\) proper flats therefore cannot cover its \((2R-1)^n\) sites. A covering family of at most \(m\) flats must contain \(\mathbb R^n\) itself, whose occupied rank is \(n\) and whose cost \(2^n(n+5)\) already exceeds \(B2^n\). Thus this theorem does not establish the locked conjecture for all bodies.
statement:
Fix an integer \(m\geq1\) and a real number \(B>0\). For every pair of positive integers \(n,d\), let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body. Use the locked notation
\(S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\) and
\(h_S(\mathbf y)=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf y}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), where the infimum is over closed ambient halfspaces. For each base point \(\mathbf z\), set
\(C_{\mathbf z}=\{\mathbf x:(\mathbf z,\mathbf x)\in C\}\) and
\(w_{\mathbf z}=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{\mathbf z})\), with empty fibers having volume zero. Assume
\(W=\mathcal H_d(S)=\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_{\mathbf z}>0\), and put
\(D_+=\{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^n:w_{\mathbf z}>0\}\) and
\(P=\operatorname{conv}(D_+)\). Suppose \(D_+=P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) be affine flats in \(\mathbb R^n\), not necessarily rational, such that
\(D_+\setminus\operatorname{Vert}(P)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^m A_i\).
For each nonempty occupied support \(E_i=D_+\cap A_i\), let
\(F_i=\operatorname{aff}(E_i)\) and \(r_i=\dim F_i\). Empty occupied supports are omitted from the following sum. Suppose

\[
\sum_{i:E_i\ne\varnothing}2^{r_i}(r_i+5)\leq B2^n.
\]

Then there is an actual point \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\), fixed before its containing halfspace is chosen, such that

\[
h_S(\mathbf y^\star)\geq c(m,B)2^{-n}W,
\qquad
c(m,B)=\min\left\{\frac{1}{e2^{m+1}},
\frac{1}{48\sqrt{15}(\ln2)B}\right\}\in(0,1/e).
\]

In particular the actual maximum depth has this lower bound, with a coefficient independent of \(n,d,C\). The marginal law, if expressed as a probability law, is the actual law \(p_{\mathbf z}=w_{\mathbf z}/W\) on \(D_+\); its depth is
\(\tau_p(\mathbf j)=\inf_{Q\ni\mathbf j}\sum_{\mathbf z\in D_+\cap Q}p_{\mathbf z}\) over proper closed base halfspaces. The predecessor aliases used below are \(h_C=h_S\) and \(\tau(\mathbf j)=W\tau_p(\mathbf j)\) in accepted fact `0bcc51d8cd216cf3`. The body conclusion of accepted fact `3bcbf21f33edf564` will be applied to each actual transformed slice, with its integer dimension equal to \(r_i\), its body equal to that slice, and its total mixed volume equal to \(\sum_{\mathbf z\in E_i}w_{\mathbf z}\).
